title: Number of Distinct Roll Sequences
summary: Given an integer n , determine the total number of distinct sequences of rolls with a fair 6-sided die, such that the greatest common divisor of any two adjacent rolls is 1, and no two identical rolls are within two rolls of each other.
statement: Given an integer n , determine the total number of distinct sequences of rolls with a fair 6-sided die, such that the greatest common divisor of any two adjacent rolls is 1, and no two identical rolls are within two rolls of each other. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7 . Two sequences are considered distinct if at least one element in the sequence is different.
constraints: Each roll is an integer one through six.
Adjacent rolls must be different and coprime.
A roll must also differ from the roll two positions earlier; return the sequence count modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: The next choice depends only on the previous two roll values.
Store counts by state (last,second_last), using zero as the missing predecessor initially.
Transition to faces different from both stored values and coprime with last; shift the state and reduce modulo M.
Those state fields contain every condition involving a new roll, so the transitions generate every valid sequence exactly once.
